Excursions — where we should go this year

Sicily

An island off the toe of Italy. 3,000 years of history. An offer you can’t refuse.

Presented by Shepard Sullivan
Use → to advance
Palermo — stop one

The Capuchin
Catacombs

  • i.Friars began mummifying their dead here in the late 1500s
  • ii.8,000 bodies line the corridors, still in their clothes
  • iii.The largest collection of mummies on earth
  • iv.Nothing like it on any other class trip
€30 guided tour ≈ $34 each
Agrigento — stop two

Valley of
the Temples

  • i.Best-preserved Greek temples outside Greece
  • ii.Built from the 5th century BC by the Greek settlers who founded Akragas
  • iii.Older than the Colosseum — older than most countries
  • iv.A whole row of them, standing above the sea
€15–20 guided tour ≈ $17–23 each
Catania — stop three

Mount Etna

  • i.The tallest active volcano in Europe — about 11,000 feet
  • ii.Cable cars run most of the way up
  • iii.We stand on cooled lava, smell the sulfur, feel it rumble
  • iv.Erupting since before the temples were built
Cable car + summit the loudest quiet you’ll ever stand in
March & April — the right window

Perfect weather,
free backup

  • i.Mid-50s to mid-60s, and barely any rain
  • ii.Free art museums if it does rain
  • iii.The puppet museum, with live marionette shows
  • iv.The No Mafia Museum
  • v.Godfather villages near Etna — free to wander
The budget — the part your parents read

It costs
less

  • i.20–40% cheaper than the rest of Italy and most of Europe

  • iii.Cheap places to stay, and street markets worth flying for
  • iv.One of the safest cities in Europe to visit
Flights $650–$950 round trip
The case

Four reasons
and one volcano

Greeks, Romans, Arabs and Normans all built here. It’s all still standing — and it’s the cheapest part of Italy to see it in.

3,000Years of history
8,000Mummies underground
11,000FTOf active volcano
20–40%Cheaper than mainland Italy
Ten days — a rough shape, not a rulebook

The itinerary

1Land in Palermo. Walk around, street food, sleep.
2Historic Palermo. Catacombs, then the cathedral rooftop.
3Mondello Beach. Seafood and gelato.
4Opera dei Pupi. Puppet museum and a live show.
5Zingaro Reserve. Sea caves and kayaking.
6Free day. Rest or repeat a favorite.
7Valley of the Temples. Overnight in Agrigento.
8Mount Etna. Cable cars up — Godfather villages nearby.
9Class vote. Everyone picks the last day.
10Fly home.
In conclusion

Pick Sicily

Great food, unique activities, low prices, good weather, ancient ruins, an active volcano and real-life mummies. Something here for every person in this room.

So — vote Sicily. And maybe you won’t wake up next to a horse head.
